Proofs.Flock.Claims.Complete.CostWalk.why: cost_walk, the tactic that bounds a computation's sends by its head (Flock/Claims/Complete/Count.lean's proof of the goal SendCount), a macro that expands to repeated apply of the module's Cost lemmas, extract_lets, intro and split. It runs only inside the elaborator and does no IO, and the kernel replays every proof it builds.

Proofs.Flock.Claims.KS.PushSched.why: push_unfold and lead_unfold, local tactics that unfold the primed prover one node (a `simp only` over Lock's rightSame, leftSame, lockWith, interleaveLock, bind and oracleStrat) in the pushing chooser's proofs (firstS_push, followR_push, lead_push and the rest of the module). They run only inside the elaborator and do no IO, and the kernel replays every proof they build.

Proofs.Flock.Claims.Recursion.CallsLe.why: keep_walk, a macro that expands to repeated refine/exact of the module's keepL/keepT bind, pure and get lemmas (a logged computation keeps its log's prefix). It runs only inside the elaborator and does no IO, and the kernel replays every proof it builds.

Proofs.Flock.Claims.Recursion.CallsRep.why: tw_walk, tw_step and lw_step, macros that expand to first/repeat' over refine/exact of the module's calcCS/calcCS2 bind, pure, throw and sample lemmas (the call bound of a rep's verification). They run only inside the elaborator and do no IO, and the kernel replays every proof they build.

Proofs.Flock.Claims.Recursion.CallsTop.why: cl_step, dec_step and ret_step, macros that expand to first over refine/exact of the module's CL/Ret bind, pure and throw lemmas, and cl_bind_of and cl_head, elabs that only read the goal and fail unless its program's head is the named constant. They run only inside the elaborator, read no files and do no IO, and the kernel replays every proof they build.

Proofs.Flock.Claims.Recursion.LogWalk.why: retl_walk, the tactic (an elab) that walks RetL goals at elaboration, step by step on the logged computation's head (retlStep, in Recursion/DecodeLog.lean's proofs and the module's own). It reads no files and does no IO, and the kernel replays every proof it builds.

Proofs.Flock.Claims.ZK.FinishLigEnd.why: end_l and keep_l, local tactics (two macro_rules) that walk a Ligerito step by its head to its last squeeze (EndL) or through steps that only update its state (KeepL), trying the module's endL_*/keepL_* lemmas with refine, exact and split, in ligeritoCut_end's proof. They run only inside the elaborator and do no IO, and the kernel replays every proof they build.

Proofs.Flock.SessionLoop.Concrete.Fwd.why: fwd_walk and fwd_def, a tactic and a command that step through a computation of the verifier by its head (a let, a jump, a bind, an if or a match, and a for loop whose body always yields as a fold) to the value it returns, rewriting by the hypotheses and lemmas they are given, in the concrete statement's walks of its circuit file's parse, its public file's load, Raw.ins and Ins.setup (SessionLoop/Concrete/File.lean to Inputs.lean); fwd_def adds the value as a definition and the walk's equation as a theorem with addDecl. kernel_rfl' closes an equation under metadata with Eq.refl, and case_both cases one discriminant on both sides of an equation (Concrete/Delta.lean). They run only inside the elaborator and read or write nothing outside it, and the kernel checks every definition and proof they add.

Proofs.Flock.Soundness.Refine.OkLe.why: ok_le_walk, the tactic (an elab, over okLeStep) that walks two runs of one executable at once by their heads, closing each step with the module's okLe_bind/ite/dite/let/jp/forIn/throw lemmas (Refine/Lookups.lean's proofs that more lookup tables change nothing). It reads no files and does no IO, and the kernel replays every proof it builds.

Proofs.Flock.Soundness.Refine.Walk.why: walk_step and ret_walk, the tactics that step through a computation of the executable by its head (Refine/Setup.lean's proofs of the setups' well-formedness), and kernel_rfl, which leaves an equation to the kernel (Composed/TagsJ.lean). They run only inside the elaborator and do no IO, and the kernel replays every proof they build.

Proofs.Pouw.Dimension.Lifting.why: the lifting worker's grid-density and slice lemmas (L2, L3) stand alone on Mathlib

loomis-whitney.about: the discrete Loomis-Whitney inequality, proved by hand

A1-johnson-mca.about: Assumptions.BCHKS25Thm46 (A1): the Johnson-range MCA bound the Ligerito folds assume

udr-mca.about: the unique-decoding fallback for the MCA bound

list-size.about: ListSize.closeMsgs_card_le: the Johnson list bound, 25·2^r at rate 2^-r

tensor-fold.about: the fold union in LigeritoLevels (2^k - 1 pairs per level, paper Lemma 9)

novel-basis.about: Arith.Correct.xhat_poly, proved per instance for L ≤ 40 (level3)

collision-resistance.about: SHA512CRStrict (cr/sha-512) and SHA512CRExpected (ecr/sha-512, A2), and the explicit collision finders

rom-cr.about: the random-oracle shadow of SHA512CRStrict (the birthday bound) and SHA512CRExpected (an expected-query birthday bound)

A3-uniform-bytes.about: A3 (UniformRandomBytes, and per test UniformRandomBytesTest, uniform/io-getrandombytes): the operating system's bytes, which the live draw and the firewall's frame and tap read through IO.getRandomBytes and the prover reads as salts through getrandom(2), are independent and uniform, per test up to eta; it rests on Linux's CRNG (drivers/char/random.c, 5.18 and later) and its reseed on a VM generation change (vmgenid), without which a restored snapshot reuses pads

hm96-hiding.about: Claims.Hm96Hiding (zero knowledge's T1, hash-derived-key): (M·y, H(sp‖y)) is δ₁-close to (U, H(sp‖y)), the leftover hash lemma at the pinned key

pad-nonvanishing.about: Assumptions.PadNonvanishing (zero knowledge): X_L + κ ≠ 0 on the level-0 domain, since Ŵ_cols(ω_q) is bit cols of q

hm-row-computes.about: HmRowComputes (circuit/hm96-sha512-row): the sha512x3 and hm96 slots compute SHA-512 and hm96's commit string, the value binding's circuit side (phase 2i)

live-verifier-custody.about: Assumptions.Zk.RecordCustodyZK (live-verifier): the record flock-verify verify --zk reads is the one the verifier's coin server wrote for the live session, and its draw file the one flock-verify draw printed for the verifier's own draw (PROTOCOL.md §17.2: nothing in the record authenticates its writer)

live-verifier-custody-tables.about: Assumptions.Zk.RecordCustodyZKJ (live-verifier): RecordCustodyZK at J tables, the record flock-verify verify --zk --session-tables J reads is the one the verifier's coin server wrote for the live session, and its draw file the one flock-verify draw printed for the verifier's own subset draw (PROTOCOL.md §17.2: nothing in the record authenticates its writer)

A4-prf-sha512.about: A4 (KeyedStreamsUniform, prf/sha-512): verity.randomness's keyed streams at distinct indices pass a test as independent uniform streams do, up to eta, SHA-512's compression function keyed by a secret first block or by its chaining value being a PRF

live-verifier-custody-exec.about: Assumptions.RecordCustodyExec and RecordCustodyExecH (live-verifier): the record flock-verify verify reads without --zk is the one the verifier's coin server wrote for the live session, and its draw file proves the drawn units with the outcome's link points (PROTOCOL.md §17.2: nothing in the record authenticates its writer)

live-verifier-custody-zk-law.about: Assumptions.Zk.RecordCustodyZKLaw, RecordCustodyZKHLaw, RecordCustodyZKJLaw and RecordCustodyZKHJLaw (live-verifier): the record flock-verify verify --zk reads is the one the verifier's coin server wrote for the live session, and at every draw of the live law its draw file proves the drawn units with the outcome's link points (PROTOCOL.md §17.2: nothing in the record authenticates its writer)
